facts.text: The Tribunal dealt with a 19 July 2017 letter as part of a course of conduct that included the builder’s correspondence.
The Tribunal concluded that there was an agreement between the parties.
In post-hearing submissions, the builder did not specifically cite Butler v Fairclough.
In post-hearing submissions, the builder cited Haller.
The Tribunal cited Haller at [20] of the Reasons.
Leave to appeal is not required in respect of Ground 6.
Ground 6 concerns whether the Tribunal made an error of law in finding the completion date of works under the parties’ 2009 contract was 20 October 2010.
Ground 7 concerns whether leave to appeal should be granted because the Tribunal’s completion date finding was against the weight of evidence.
The owners argued that practical completion under the original contract took place on 20 October 2010 when the FOC issued.
The Tribunal agreed with the thrust of the owners' submission about practical completion taking place when the FOC issued.
The contract was a 2009 contract.
The completion date of the works under the 2009 contract was found to be 20 October 2010.
The contract was described as a standard form Housing Industry Association (HIA) contract.

Clause 1 of the contract defines “building works” as the building works to be carried out, completed and handed over to the owner in accordance with the contract as shown in the contract documents and including variations.

Clause 1 defines “practical completion” as when the building works are complete except for minor omissions and defects that do not prevent the building works from being reasonably capable of being used for their usual purpose.
Clause 7 of the contract is headed “Planning and Building Approvals”.
Clause 7.1 requires the party named in Item 11 of Schedule 1 to obtain and pay for all building and planning approvals.
Item 11 names the builder as the responsible party for the purposes of clause 7.
The builder was responsible for obtaining the FOC.
The builder’s obligation to provide the FOC fell within the definition of “building works” under the contract.
Completion of the works occurred within the meaning of the contract for the purposes of s 3B(1) of the HB Act upon the owners’ receipt of the Final Occupation Certificate (FOC).
The Tribunal’s completion-date finding was relevant to its finding that there was consideration in respect of the new contract it found the parties had entered into.
The Tribunal concluded that it erred in its interpretation of relevant terms of the contract.
The Tribunal’s reasoning process concluded that the builder’s obligation to provide the FOC was part of “building works” and that completion occurred upon the owners’ receipt of the FOC.
The Tribunal’s reasoning process concluded that the builder’s responsibility for obtaining the FOC supported the completion-date conclusion.
The Tribunal’s reasoning process concluded that the completion-date finding was relevant to consideration for the new contract.
The Tribunal’s reasoning process stated that it was not strictly necessary to consider Ground 6 and 7 given findings in respect of Grounds 2 and 3, but it did so for completeness.
The owners received the FOC as part of planning and building approvals under item 11 in Schedule 1.
The text states that a date is not required, just a specified activity, for the completion date under the contract interpretation.
The text references HBA s 3B(1), s 3B(2), and s 3B(3).

events.text: Tribunal dealt with the 19 July 2017 letter as part of a course of conduct leading to a conclusion of agreement
Practical completion under the original contract took place on 20 October 2010 when the FOC issued (as argued by the owners)
Completion date of the works under the 2009 contract was found to be 20 October 2010 (Ground 6 issue)
